stemMd:
In the eight months after the regional tourism board launched a multilingual website, overnight stays by foreign visitors in the region's hotels rose by 9 percent. The board concludes that the website attracted additional foreign visitors to the region.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the board's conclusion?

options.label: A
options.textMd: In a similar neighbouring region with no new website, foreign overnight stays did not change in those months.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The new website is available in five languages, one more than the website of the neighbouring region.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Overnight stays by domestic visitors in the region also rose by about 9 percent over the same eight months.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Most foreign visitors who stayed in the region's hotels had booked through travel agencies rather than online.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The tourism board employs three full-time staff who work only on the multilingual website and its translations.

explanationMd:
The board moves from "the number rose after the launch" to "the launch caused the rise". The weak point is that something else may have raised the number in the same months: a strong season, a favourable exchange rate, a general recovery in travel. The strongest supporting evidence is therefore a **comparison** that rules such causes out.

A similar neighbouring region offers exactly that. It shared the same season and the same travel conditions but did not launch a website, and its foreign stays did not change. If the general conditions had lifted foreign visits, that region would have risen too. This makes the website a much better explanation of the regional rise.

The other choices either point toward a general upswing (domestic visitors also rising), suggest the website was not how visitors booked (travel agencies), or say nothing about cause at all (number of languages, size of the web team).

distractorRationale.c: This weakens the conclusion. A rise of the same size among domestic visitors, who are not the target of a multilingual website, suggests a general upswing that would explain the foreign increase without the website.
distractorRationale.b: A comparison of the number of languages says nothing about whether visitors came because of the site. It gives no evidence that the website changed anyone's decision.
distractorRationale.d: This weakens the conclusion, because it suggests that the website was not how most foreign visitors found or chose the region.
distractorRationale.e: Full-time staff and careful translations show the board takes the website seriously, not that the site changed the number of foreign visitors.

accessibilityText: An argument question about strengthening a conclusion. A regional tourism board says overnight stays by foreign visitors rose by 9 percent in the eight months after it launched a multilingual website, and concludes that the website attracted additional foreign visitors. The question asks which statement most strengthens that conclusion. The choices: in a similar neighbouring region with no new website, foreign overnight stays did not change in those months; the new site is in five languages, one more than the neighbouring region's; domestic overnight stays also rose about 9 percent over the same months; most foreign visitors booked through travel agencies rather than online; three full-time staff work only on the site and its translations.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank. Scenario, names and figures are invented; no published TOLC or other test item was used or adapted.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The conclusion is causal, so the best strengthener is a control. A similar neighbouring region with no new website saw no change, which rules out a general trend. Domestic stays rising by the same 9 percent points to a general trend and weakens the conclusion. Most foreign visitors booking through agencies rather than online weakens it. The number of languages and the staffing are irrelevant to whether the website caused the rise. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-cue-batch2-run1) reached the same answer: A comparable neighbouring region without a new website saw no change, which acts as a control and rules out a general tourism trend. The five-languages fact and the dedicated staff are irrelevant to effect; domestic stays rising equally suggests a general trend (weakens); bookings mainly through agencies rather than online also weakens.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: only the control-region comparison supplies evidence that the rise is not due to general conditions. Two of the distractors weaken the conclusion and two are irrelevant. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key. Choices rebalanced on 2026-09-29 to remove an answer-length cue; the key is unchanged.
